subject: Scalable addendum & usage economics — Q1 health and extension options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@ornate.ai>, Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@ornate.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Scalable addendum & usage economics — Q1 health and extension options

Hi Ana / Tom —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. I pulled together a short usage health recap and a proposal for a lightweight addendum that would give Ornate a flexible capacity corridor plus an incremental add-on lane for spike months. High level:

- Q1 token burn: ~3.9M tokens/month average, 6.8M peak (concentrated around weekly batch jobs)
- Observed p95 generation latency on current instance type: 550ms (we can get this to ~380ms with a small instance bump + smarter batch shaping)
- Current committed run-rate covers ~70% of steady-state usage; spikes cause burst costs of ~28% over baseline spend

Attached: Q1_usage_summary.csv (export), latency_trends_Q1.png (dashboard snippet), and a draft addendum (proposed_addendum_v2.docx).

Proposed addendum highlights:
1) Flexible corridor: baseline commit = 4.5M tokens/mo, corridor up to 7M tokens/mo billed at a blended incremental rate — keeps predictability while allowing bursts.
2) Surge credit bucket: one-time 250k token spike credits for Q2 onboarding activities.
3) Performance tuning credits: 8 hours of engineering support to implement batching/kv-cache heuristics (we estimate 15–25% token savings for your summarization pipelines).

Next steps I'd propose: you and Tom review the addendum text, Marissa will run the 12-month ROI projection with the new blended rates, and Monica can coordinate procurement language for the SOW add-on. Can you share any internal procurement deadlines?

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — thanks, this is really helpful. Quick clarifying Qs:

1) The peak months are driven by nightly batch enrich jobs (3am PST) that fan out a high number of short-generation calls. Is the surge credit intended to absorb replays in Q2 or true traffic-driven surges?
2) Can you share the ROI framing that assumes the performance tuning credits — we need a sense of time-to-payback before Ops signs off.

Procurement timeline: our Q2 budget cycle closes April 20th; best-case we need an agreement signed by April 5th to ensure lane in next month's invoice.

If helpful, we can sync a short 20-min call with Tom + procurement on Tuesday.

Thanks —
Ana Ruiz
Head of Product Ops, Ornate AI

Ana — quick ROI sketch attached; pulled numbers from your Q1 export and applied the blended corridor rates and performance tuning assumptions. Key bullets:

- Baseline annualized spend today (extrapolated): $190k
- If we adopt the proposed corridor + 250k surge credits + performance tuning, projected annualized spend = $168k (net savings ~11.6%)
- If tuning hits upper estimate (25% token reduction on summarization pipeline) we model ~28% reduction vs current by month 6 (includes one-time tuning credit amortized)
- Latency improvement estimate: 550ms -> ~380ms p95 after instance bump + batching changes; this reduces timeouts on 3rd-party enrich jobs and should cut replays ~40% (we modeled replay reduction into the ROI).

Attachment: ROI_runway_orate_v1.xlsx (summary) — note: I used conservative uplift for non-summarization pipelines (10%).

If that looks reasonable I can finalize the 12-month pro forma and push the addendum into the legal queue. Karthik — want me to include a 30/60/90 milestone appendix tied to tuning deliverables?

Marissa
